summary: Robert P. Weller is a scholar in sinology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Johns Hopkins University (1975–1981) and became a professor at Boston University in 1990.

Robert Paget Dewhurst was an Indology, Iranian and Central Asian, and linguistics scholar. He earned an M.A. from the University of Oxford in 1888, where he later served as University Lecturer in Hindustani in 1924.

Robert Ripley Moore worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Bethel College (B.A., to 1956) and the University of Michigan (Ph.D., to 1965), later teaching at Mussoorie College and serving as Assistant Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1966).

Robert S. Ellwood worked in religious studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Colorado, Yale University, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade, later holding a post at the University of Southern California (~1967–1997).

Robert S. Nelson is a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Rice University (~1965–1969) and New York University (~1969–1978). He held professorships at the University of Chicago (~1974–2005) and posts at Yale University (~2005–2021).

Robert S. P. Beekes specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (~1956–1969) under doctoral supervisor F. B. J. Kuiper, and held posts at the Marnix Gymnasium and Leiden University (1973, 1979).

Robert Schram worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned a Ph.D. and PD at the University of Vienna (1869–1874) and held posts at Geneva Observatory (1872–1873), Militärgeographisches Institut (1887), and the University of Vienna (~1887).

Robert Sewell was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who attended Radley College (~1858–1863). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1868–1894) and held positions as Keeper at Tamil Nadu Archives and Fellow at the University of Madras.
Robert Seymour Conway was a linguist who studied at the City of London School (~1876–1883). He later held posts at Newnham College, Cambridge (~1887–1893) and Gonville and Caius College (~1888–1894).

Robert Tegethoff is an Iranian and Central Asian, linguistics, and Indology scholar. He earned an M.A. from the University of Cologne (2015–2018) and held posts at the Free University of Berlin, including as a postdoc in 2026.
Robert Vane Russell worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1891–1894) and served in the Indian Civil Service (~1895–1915).
Robert Warren Clark is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Karen Christina Lang and adviser K. L. Seshagiri Rao (both attested 1994).

Robert Watson Frazer was an Indologist educated at Rathmines School and Trinity College Dublin under Robert Atkinson. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1877–1886) and lectured on Telugu and Tamil at UCL (1885–1916) and SOAS (1917–1919).
Robert Wilson Ievers was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar. He earned an M.A. from Queen's University Belfast and served as a civil servant in the Ceylon Civil Service starting in 1872.

Robert Xavier Murphy worked in Indology, linguistics, and history and archaeology. He served as master at the Bombay Native Education Society (~1830–1839) and secretary at the Bombay Chamber of Commerce and Industry in 1839.

Robert Zimmermann was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies scholar. Educated at St Beuno's and Berlin (Ph.D. 1913) under Heinrich Lüders, he founded the Maha Bodhi Society, directed BORI, and was professor at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1914–1930).

Robert Zydenbos specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at Utrecht University (~1975–1989), he held posts at the University of Munich (~2003), University of Toronto, and Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Robert van Gulik was a scholar of sinology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden and Utrecht under C. C. Uhlenbeck, J. J. L. Duyvendak, and Jan Gonda, later becoming professor at Utrecht University in 1967.

Robert von Heine-Geldern was an Indology and archaeology scholar educated at Munich and Vienna under Wilhelm Schmidt. He held posts at the University of Vienna, Columbia University, Asia Institute, and American Museum of Natural History.

Robert von Schlagintweit worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at the University of Munich (~1851–1854) and was appointed Professor of Geography at the University of Giessen in 1864.
